subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath caches inside plugin hook, plugin skill, and sandbox host-path containment checks once the linked PR is buildable and proof is refreshed?
rationale: The performance fix changes cache lifetime around realpath-based containment checks, which is narrower than the proposed process-wide cache but still security-boundary-sensitive.

options.title: Accept operation-scoped caches after repair
options.body: Fix the duplicate export, refresh focused and Windows proof, and accept per-operation cache maps as the intended performance/security tradeoff.

options.title: Reject caching in containment checks
options.body: Keep containment checks fully fresh and move performance work to non-boundary metadata/discovery paths only.

options.title: Pause for a narrower contract
options.body: Define exactly which callers may reuse realpath answers and require the linked PR to match that contract before review continues.

recommendation.title: Accept operation-scoped caches after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the duplicate export, refresh focused and Windows proof, and accept per-operation cache maps as the intended performance/security tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the linked PR and recently handled the narrower manifest-registry realpath cache follow-up.
